constraints: Opt-in only: the Oracle path is selected by an explicit `oracleResolution: { maxMaterializedBytes }` option; without it behavior is unchanged.
Requirements are derived only from declared BackendWorkOrder.requiredFiles and QaWorkOrder.requiredArtifacts; Oracle never adds or drops context.

The Oracle path composes only delivered @exharness/oracle root exports: createSourceCatalog, createExactRepositoryProvider, createExactArtifactProvider, createRetrievalPlanner, createOracleContextResolver, assertConsumableContextResolution.
Research consumes the BB-087 fixed-facade desired state; the Worker binds only DONE BB-087.
Any unresolved declared context blocks before Worker execution with a typed error, exactly like a compatibility read failure.
invariants: The Application alone decides required context; the Oracle path resolves exactly the declared files/artifacts and nothing else.
On identical inputs the Oracle path returns a context deep-equal to the compatibility path, including sourceRef and QA acceptance provenance.
Unresolved, partial, stale, provenance-mismatched or over-budget declared context never reaches a Worker.
Without the opt-in option, Backend and QA behavior and outputs are unchanged.
architectureDecisions: D1 — Add packages/agentic-system/src/oracle-context-requirements.js exporting backendContextRequirement(order, {maxMaterializedBytes}), qaContextRequirement(order, {maxMaterializedBytes}), projectBackendContext(order, resolution) and projectQaContext(order, resolution). packages/agentic-system/src/oracle.js gains an optional `oracleResolution` option on resolveBackendContext/resolveQaContext and branches to the Oracle path only when it is present.

D2 — Backend requirement: consumerRef `backend-work-order:<workOrderId>`, one REQUIRED evidence per required file in declared order with id `file-<index>`, source {kind REPOSITORY, ref repositoryRef, snapshot {mode EXACT, ref revision}, itemRefs [path]}; budget {maxItems n, maxProviderCalls n, maxResolutionSteps 1, maxMaterializedBytes caller value}. A non-positive or missing maxMaterializedBytes is rejected.

D3 — QA requirement: one REQUIRED evidence per required artifact, source {kind APPLICATION_ARTIFACT, ref artifact.ref, snapshot {mode EXACT, ref upstream.revision}, itemRefs [artifact.path]}. The Oracle QA path requires every artifact to declare a path (the delivered QA objective flow always selects artifacts by path); a pathless artifact is rejected with a typed error and remains supported only on the compatibility path.

D4 — Per-call composition: the adapter builds a SourceCatalog with exactly one exact provider — createExactRepositoryProvider({repositoryReader}) or createExactArtifactProvider({artifactReader, producerWorkOrderId, acceptanceDecision}) from the order — plus an EXACT snapshot authority whose observe() returns the order's pinned revision, then createRetrievalPlanner and createOracleContextResolver. EXACT mode claims no currentness; the pinned revision is the order's accepted revision.

D5 — Consumption: the adapter calls assertConsumableContextResolution(resolution, requirement) and additionally requires status COMPLETE (all evidence is REQUIRED). Otherwise it throws `backend|qa context resolution failed via Oracle: <status> <evidenceId>:<reason>...` before any Worker call.

D6 — Projection: items are grouped by evidenceId in declared order; each item's content and SOURCE_REF provenance ref become {path, content, sourceRef}; QA artifacts add {ref, path, provenance:{sourceClass APPLICATION_ARTIFACT, producerWorkOrderId, acceptanceDecision}} exactly as readApplicationArtifacts does, then the unchanged schemas parse the result.

D7 — Manifest protection: when artifactReader is createManifestArtifactReader, the exact artifact provider calls readApplicationArtifacts with the same producer/revision/acceptance arguments, so manifest validation runs unchanged; digest or provenance mismatch surfaces as provider SOURCE_FAILURE and blocks via D5.

D8 — Intended difference: the Oracle path enforces maxMaterializedBytes; the compatibility path has no budget. Over-budget declared context is BUDGET_EXHAUSTED -> UNSATISFIED -> blocked. This is documented, not hidden.
D9 — Equivalence is proven by a shared fixture test that runs both paths for Backend and QA (direct reader and manifest-validating reader) and asserts deepEqual contexts.
D10 — Worker-start: BB-087 DONE; verify the listed Oracle root exports and that the fixed facade reports exact materializedBytes; mismatch => PLAN_INPUT_CONTRADICTION.
implementationSlices: A1 — Requirement mapping [AD1, AD2, INV-1]: implement backendContextRequirement and qaContextRequirement per D2-D3 with unit tests for evidence order, EXACT snapshot, itemRefs, budget and pathless-artifact rejection.

A2 — Oracle path [AD1, AD2, AD3]: implement per-call composition, consumption and projection per D4-D6 and the opt-in branch in oracle.js; tests for COMPLETE projection and every blocking status/reason.

A3 — Equivalence + manifest [AD3, AD4, INV-2, INV-4]: equivalence test runs compatibility and Oracle paths on shared Backend and QA fixtures, including a createManifestArtifactReader-backed QA fixture with a tampered artifact, and asserts deepEqual outputs or identical blocking.

A4 — Living truth [AD4]: export the new helpers from index.js, update docs/living/system/oracle/workflow.md to describe the opt-in Oracle path and its budget difference, and run agentic/Oracle/repository regressions.

negativeVerificationCases: Calling resolveBackendContext/resolveQaContext without oracleResolution must never construct an Oracle catalog or resolver.
A missing, zero or negative maxMaterializedBytes is rejected before resolution.
An Oracle requirement containing a file or artifact not declared by the order, or omitting one, fails the mapping test.
A pathless QA artifact on the Oracle path fails with a typed error; the same order on the compatibility path still resolves.
A repository or artifact reader failure on the Oracle path blocks with SOURCE_FAILURE before any Worker call.
A manifest-protected artifact whose bytes were changed blocks on the Oracle path exactly as on the compatibility path.
Declared context larger than maxMaterializedBytes yields BUDGET_EXHAUSTED and blocks; it is never truncated and passed to a Worker.
Oracle and compatibility contexts that differ in path, content, sourceRef, order or QA provenance fail the equivalence test.
Edits to Oracle package, Worker, schema, application or manifest files fail repository scope verification.
